KEY MESSAGE 1: Extreme/Excessive heat will remain a concern into
early next week.

UPDATE: The forecast for today was updated to better reflect
better sea breeze timing and possible influences on how 
dewpoints will pool at the coast. Dewpoints were lowered 
slightly well inland where a bit more mixing is expected, but 
were raised a degree or so along/behind the sea breeze where 
guidance is in pretty good agreement on its timing and 
structure. Expect max heat indices to peak 112 to 118 at the 
coast and a few spots could make a run for the 120 degree mark. 
Farther inland, heat indices will peak 105-112 (lowest closest 
to east- central GA, the CSRA and Southern Midlands). There is 
concern that 112+ heat indices will reach interior portions of 
Liberty and Bryan Counties, so trends there will be monitored in
case the Extreme Heat Warning needs to be expanded into these 
areas. For now, status quo was maintained until trends can be 
better established.

Today into Next Week: A large-scale ridge across much of the South 
Central United States will expand eastward today through late week, 
becoming centered across the Deep South and Southeast United States 
and favoring a warm west/northwesterly aloft. Ample sunshine will 
promote strong sfc heating during the next couple days, with 1000-
850 mb thickness levels supportive of afternoon highs in the mid-
upper 90s, with some locations touching 100 degrees away from the 
coast through much of the weekend. In addition to hot temperatures, 
conditions will be quite humid with sfc dewpts in the mid-upper 70s 
each day. Although some mixing out of sfc dewpts is anticipated 
inland with the downslope wind setup locally, a sea breeze will 
eventually shift higher moisture content onshore each day for at 
least a few hours. This will likely result in the higher 
heat/moisture combination along coastal zones (along/east of I-95) 
for the next couple days, with heat index values up to the 110-115 
range this afternoon and again Friday afternoon. Further inland, 
heat index values should top out in the 105-110 degree range. Given 
the setup and expected heat index values, an Extreme Heat Warning 
remains in effect for coastal counties from 11 AM to 8 PM today 
while remaining areas are included in a Heat Advisory for the same 
time period. The slightly more favorable position of the synoptic 
ridge supports slightly higher heat index values along the coastal 
corridor Friday. Therefore, an Extreme Heat Watch has been issued 
for all Southeast SC/GA coastal zones from 11 AM to 8 PM Friday 
afternoon. Another Heat Advisory could be needed for inland areas on 
Friday as well.  

Hot/humid conditions likely remain across the Southeast United 
States late weekend into early next week with the large-scale ridge 
centered over or nearby, although a front could lead to greater 
shower/thunderstorm coverage that limits maximum heat conditions. 
Additional heat headlines could be needed through early next
week. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: There is a risk of strong thunderstorms today.

Strong ridging aloft will persist over the southeastern states today 
while a shortwave ripples across the northern periphery of the 
ridge. CAMs have struggled the last few days to get a handle on 
convection given the northwesterly flow at the surface, but the 
shortwave could be enough forcing to trigger thunderstorms across 
the SC Midlands. The latest runs of the HRRR and the 00Z HREF depict 
some convection firing in the later afternoon hours and tracking 
into the SC Lowcountry and Southeastern GA into the evening. 
Additionally, isolated convection is possible with the afternoon sea 
breeze. Unlike on Wednesday, the sea breeze shouldn't be pinned at 
the coast and looks to be progressive this afternoon. The forecast 
features slight chance thunderstorms this afternoon. Any storms that 
are able to form or track into the forecast area have the chance to 
become strong. The environment this afternoon is forecast to have
DCAPE values upwards of 1000 J/kg. The main threat this afternoon
would be damaging wind gusts with any of the stronger thunderstorms.
